questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an allotrope of Carbon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbon dioxide**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Diamond, Fullerenes, and Graphite** are all allotropes of carbon.
 
• An allotrope is a different structural form of the same element, where the atoms are bonded together in different ways.
 
• **Carbon dioxide** is a compound consisting of carbon and oxygen atoms and is not an allotrope of carbon.
 
• Allotropes of carbon exhibit different physical and chemical properties despite being composed of the same element.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Diamond** is a hard, transparent crystal where each carbon atom is bonded to four other carbon atoms in a tetrahedral structure.
 
• **Graphite** is a soft, opaque allotrope where each carbon atom is bonded to three other carbon atoms in layers of hexagonal structures, which can slide over each other.
 
• **Fullerenes** are molecules composed entirely of carbon, taking the form of hollow spheres, ellipsoids, or tubes.
 
• Carbon can also form other allotropes, such as graphene, which is a single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a hexagonal lattice.

questions.question: Which allotrope of carbon is in the form of the geodesic dome?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__ ____fullerene__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The fullerene allotrope of carbon is in the form of a geodesic globe__.

 __
 
• Fullerene is the allotrope of carbon that has a geodesic dome-like structure.
 
• Fullerene is identified as C-60 which has carbon atoms arranged in the shape of a football.
 
• Since this looked like the geodesic dome designed by the US architect Buckminster Fuller, the molecule was named Fullerene.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Carbon nanotubes are tubes made of carbon with diameters typically measured in nanometers.

 
 
• Carbon nanotubes often refer to single-wall carbon nanotubes with diameters in the range of a nanometer.
 
• Single-wall carbon nanotubes are one of the allotropes of carbon, intermediate between fullerene cages and flat graphene.
 
 
 
• Diamond is a solid form of the element carbon with its atoms arranged in a crystal structure called diamond cubic.
 
 
• At room temperature and pressure, another solid form of carbon known as graphite is the chemically stable form of carbon, but diamond converts to it extremely slowly.
 
 
 
• Graphite is a crystalline form of the element carbon with its atoms arranged in a hexagonal structure
 
 
• It occurs naturally in this form and is the most stable form of carbon under standard conditions.
 
• Graphite is used in pencils and lubricants.

questions.question: Regarding carbon, which of the following statements is true?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbon is tetravalent**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Carbon has four valence electrons, allowing it to form four covalent bonds with other atoms.
 
• This tetravalent nature of carbon is fundamental to the chemistry of life, as it enables the formation of complex molecules like carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids.
 
• Carbon can form single, double, and triple bonds, increasing the diversity and complexity of carbon-based compounds.
 
• The ability to form long carbon chains and rings is unique to carbon, making it the backbone of organic chemistry.
 
• Carbon's tetravalency allows it to bond with various elements, including hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, and sulfur, further expanding the range of possible organic molecules.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Allotropes of Carbon**

 
 
• Carbon exists in several allotropes, including diamond, graphite, graphene, and fullerenes, each with distinct properties.
 
• In diamond, carbon atoms are arranged in a tetrahedral lattice, making it extremely hard.
 
• In graphite, carbon atoms are arranged in layers of hexagonal lattices, making it a good conductor of electricity.
 
 
 
• **Carbon Cycle**
 
 
• The carbon cycle is the process by which carbon moves through the atmosphere, hydrosphere, biosphere, and geosphere.
 
• It plays a crucial role in regulating Earth's climate and supporting life by recycling carbon dioxide and organic carbon.
 
 
 
• **Carbon Dating**
 
 
• Carbon dating, or radiocarbon dating, is a method used to determine the age of ancient artifacts and fossils.
 
• It is based on the decay of carbon-14, a radioactive isotope of carbon, to nitrogen-14 over time.

questions.question: Carbon has the unique ability to form bonds with other atoms of carbon. This property is known as ______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**catenation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Catenation** is the ability of an element to form bonds with other atoms of the same element.
 
• Carbon atoms can form long chains and rings due to their ability to catenate.
 
• This property allows carbon to form a vast number of compounds, more than any other element.
 
• Catenation is a crucial property for the formation of organic molecules, including hydrocarbons and polymers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tetravalency of Carbon:**

 
 
• Carbon has four valence electrons, allowing it to form four covalent bonds with other atoms, including other carbon atoms.
 
 
 
• **Hydrocarbons:**
 
 
• Compounds composed solely of carbon and hydrogen. They are categorized into alkanes, alkenes, and alkynes based on the types of bonds between carbon atoms.
 
 
 
• **Isomerism:**
 
 
• Carbon compounds can exhibit isomerism, where compounds have the same molecular formula but different structural arrangements.
 
 
 
• **Polymerization:**
 
 
• Carbon compounds can undergo polymerization, where small monomer units join to form large polymers, such as plastics and biological macromolecules.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements regarding saturated and unsaturated carbon compounds is correct?

Statement I: Saturated carbon compounds are hydrocarbons where carbon atoms are connected by single covalent bonds.

Statement II: Unsaturated carbon compounds are hydrocarbons where carbon atoms are connected by single covalent bonds.

options.text: Neither statement I nor II is correct.
Both statements I and II are correct.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Only statement I is correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Saturated carbon compounds** are hydrocarbons where carbon atoms are connected by **single covalent bonds**.
 
• These compounds are typically **alkanes**.
 
• **Unsaturated carbon compounds** are hydrocarbons where carbon atoms are connected by **double or triple covalent bonds**.
 
• These compounds include **alkenes** (with double bonds) and **alkynes** (with triple bonds).
 
• Statement I correctly describes saturated carbon compounds.
 
• Statement II incorrectly describes unsaturated carbon compounds as having single covalent bonds, which is characteristic of saturated compounds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Saturated hydrocarbons**__

 __
 
• These are **aliphatic hydrocarbons** like **methane, ethane, and propane**.
 
• They are generally **less reactive** than unsaturated hydrocarbons.
 
 
 
• **Unsaturated hydrocarbons**__
 
 
• These compounds include **ethene (ethylene)** and **ethyne (acetylene)**.
 
• They are more **reactive** due to the presence of multiple bonds.

questions.question: A series of compounds in which the same functional group substitutes for hydrogen in a carbon chain is called _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**homologous series**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **homologous series** is a group of organic compounds that have a similar general formula and possess similar chemical properties.
 
• In a homologous series, each successive member differs by a **-CH2- unit**.
 
• The members of a homologous series are called **homologues**.
 
• Homologous series exhibit a gradual change in **physical properties** such as boiling point, melting point, and density.
 
• Examples of homologous series include **alkanes, alkenes, and alkynes**.
 
• One notable characteristic is that the **functional group** remains the same throughout the series.
 
• Homologous series are important in organic chemistry because they help in the systematic study and prediction of properties of organic compounds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Isomers**__

 __
 
• **Isomers** are compounds that have the same molecular formula but different structural arrangements.
 
• Isomers can be classified into **structural isomers** and **stereoisomers**.
 
• Structural isomers have different connectivity of atoms, while stereoisomers have the same connectivity but differ in spatial arrangement.
 
 
 
• **Isochores**__
 __
 
• **Isochores** are regions of DNA with a high degree of uniformity in base composition.
 
• They are significant in the field of genetics and genomics.
 
 
 
• **Isobars**__
 
 
• **Isobars** are atoms of different chemical elements that have the same number of nucleons.
 
• Isobars differ in chemical properties because they have different atomic numbers.

questions.question: What type of bonding is present in carbon compounds?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Covalent Bonding**.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Carbon forms** covalent bonds.
 
• There are **three major types of covalent bonds:** single, double, and triple bonds.
 
• **A carbon atom can form four single bonds.**
 
• A Covalent bond is a bond that is formed after the sharing of electron pairs between atoms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Metallic Bonding:**

 
 
• **Metallic bonding occurs when metal atoms share their valence electrons freely in a "sea of electrons." **
 
• This bonding explains the properties of metals such as electrical conductivity, malleability, and ductility.
 
• **Example: Copper (Cu)**
 
• Copper atoms bond together with metallic bonds, allowing electrons to move freely, giving copper its excellent electrical conductivity.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen Bonding:**
 
 
• **Hydrogen bonding occurs when hydrogen is covalently bonded to a highly electronegative element like nitrogen, oxygen, or fluorine,** and is attracted to a lone pair of electrons on another electronegative atom.
 
• **Example: Water (H₂O)**
 
• In water, hydrogen bonds form between the hydrogen atoms of one molecule and the oxygen atom of another, giving water its high boiling point and surface tension.
 
 
 
• **Ionic Bonding:**
 
 
• Ionic bonding** occurs when one atom donates an electron to another, creating positively and negatively charged ions that are attracted to each other.**
 
• **Example: Sodium chloride (NaCl)**
 
• Sodium (Na) donates an electron to chlorine (Cl), forming Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions that are held together by electrostatic forces.

questions.question: Carbon, known for its versatility, forms compounds mainly with hydrogen. However, it can also bond with others such as halogens, oxygen, nitrogen, and sulphur. When these elements replace one or more hydrogen atoms in a hydrocarbon chain, the valency of carbon remains satisfied. The thing that replaces hydrogen in such compounds is called a ____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Heteroatom**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A heteroatom is any atom that replaces hydrogen in a hydrocarbon chain and is not carbon or hydrogen.
 
• Common heteroatoms include oxygen, nitrogen, sulfur, and halogens such as chlorine, bromine, and iodine.
 
• Heteroatoms impart unique chemical properties to organic compounds, such as increased reactivity or altered polarity.
 
• They play a crucial role in forming functional groups, which determine the chemical behavior of organic molecules.
 
• Compounds containing heteroatoms are widely studied in organic chemistry, pharmaceuticals, and materials science.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Functional Groups:** Groups of atoms containing heteroatoms that define the chemical properties of organic compounds (e.g., hydroxyl, carboxyl, amino).
 
• **Valency of Carbon:** Carbon maintains its tetravalency by forming stable bonds with heteroatoms and other carbon atoms.
 
• **Polarity:** The presence of heteroatoms often introduces dipoles, making molecules polar and affecting their solubility and interactions.
 
• **Applications:** Organic compounds with heteroatoms are critical in pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, and industrial materials.
 
• **Examples:** Alcohols (OH group), amines (NH₂ group), and halogenated hydrocarbons (Cl, Br, or I atoms) showcase heteroatoms in action.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about ‘nature of a carbon compound’?

options.text: Carbon has the unique ability to form bonds with other atoms of carbon, giving rise to large molecules. This property is called catenation.
Compounds of carbon having double or triple bonds between their carbon atoms are called unsaturated compounds.
Compounds of carbon are only formed with oxygen.
Compounds of carbon, which are linked by only single bonds between the carbon atoms, are called saturated compounds.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Carbon has the unique ability to form bonds with other atoms of carbon, giving rise to large molecules. This property is called catenation.
 
• Compounds of carbon having double or triple bonds between their carbon atoms are called unsaturated compounds.
 
• Compounds of carbon, which are linked by only single bonds between the carbon atoms, are called saturated compounds.
 
• Carbon compounds can form strong bonds with other elements such as hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, and halogens. **Thus, statement 3 is incorrect.**
 
• Carbon compounds can exist in various forms, including chains, branched chains, and rings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alkanes**

 
 
• These are saturated hydrocarbons with single bonds between carbon atoms.
 
• They follow the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.
 
 
 
• **Alkenes**
 
 
• These are unsaturated hydrocarbons with at least one double bond between carbon atoms.
 
• They follow the general formula CₙH₂ₙ.
 
 
 
• **Alkynes**
 
 
• These are unsaturated hydrocarbons with at least one triple bond between carbon atoms.
 
• They follow the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₋₂.

questions.question: A sucrose molecule contains ______ carbon atoms.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**12**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A sucrose molecule is composed of two monosaccharides: glucose and fructose.
 
• Glucose and fructose are both hexose sugars, meaning they each contain six carbon atoms.
 
• When glucose (C6H12O6) and fructose (C6H12O6) combine to form sucrose, a water molecule (H2O) is removed.
 
• Therefore, the molecular formula of sucrose is C12H22O11, indicating that it contains 12 carbon atoms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Monosaccharides**

 
 
• These are the simplest form of carbohydrates and cannot be hydrolyzed to simpler chemical compounds.
 
• Examples include glucose, fructose, and galactose.
 
• Monosaccharides are the building blocks of more complex sugars such as disaccharides and polysaccharides.
 
 
 
• **Disaccharides**
 
 
• These are carbohydrates formed by the combination of two monosaccharides.
 
• Examples include sucrose (glucose + fructose), lactose (glucose + galactose), and maltose (glucose + glucose).
 
• They are broken down into their constituent monosaccharides during digestion.
 
 
 
• **Polysaccharides**
 
 
• These are large, complex carbohydrates composed of long chains of monosaccharide units.
 
• Examples include starch, glycogen, and cellulose.
 
• They serve various functions such as energy storage (starch, glycogen) and structural support (cellulose in plants).
 
 
 
• **Hydrolysis**
 
 
• This is a chemical process that involves the breakdown of a compound due to a reaction with water.
 
• In the context of carbohydrates, hydrolysis breaks down disaccharides and polysaccharides into monosaccharides.
 
• For example, the hydrolysis of sucrose yields glucose and fructose.

questions.question: Carbon exhibits catenation property due to _____

options.text: its small size and greater strength of carbon-carbon bond
its large size and greater strength of carbon-carbon bond
its small size and weaker strength of carbon-carbon bond
its large size and weaker strength of carbon-carbon bond

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Small size and greater strength of carbon-carbon bond.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Carbon:**

 
 
• The chemical element carbon has the a**tomic number six **and the** symbol C.**
 
• It is **nonmetallic and tetravalent,** which means that because its valence shell has four electrons, its atoms can form up to four covalent bonds.
 
• It is a member of periodic table group 14.
 
• **It is a small atom with a small atomic radius, allowing it to form strong carbon- carbon covalent bonds.**
 
• The strength of the carbon-carbon bond allows for the formation of **long chains or rings**, which is the basis of** catenation.**
 
• The strength of the bond also makes carbon compounds **more stable** and **less reactive.**
 
• Different carbon atoms can form different bonds with one another to form different carbon allotropes. **Amorphous carbon, diamond, graphite, and fullerenes are a few examples of well-known allotropes.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Catenation:**

 
 
• **The capacity of certain elements to create bonds with atoms of the same element **is known as catenation, and it's a fascinating idea in chemistry.
 
• The great diversity and complexity of organic chemistry arise from this characteristic, which is especially noticeable in carbon compounds.
 
• **Catenation's greatest champion is carbon, which has four valence electrons. It easily forms strong covalent connections with other carbon atoms to form complex structures and lengthy chains.**
 
• Carbon may produce a variety of compounds, such as alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, and aromatic compounds, by making single, double, and even triple bonds with itself.
 
• The c**atenation property of carbon is responsible for the amazing diversity of organic chemistry. **
 
• Other elements like **silicon and germanium** can also exhibit catenation, but their bonds are** not as strong** as carbon-carbon bonds.

questions.question: Buckminster fullerene, which looks like a football, is an allotropic form of
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Buckminsterfullerene**:

 
 
• **Fullerene is a carbon allotrope** consisting of fused rings of five to seven atoms and a molecule composed of carbon atoms linked by single and double bonds to form a closed or partially closed lattice.
 
• Buckminsterfullerene has the formula C60 and is a type of fullerene.
 
• It is composed of twenty hexagons and twelve pentagons and has a cage-like fused-ring structure (truncated icosahedron) that resembles a soccer ball.
 
• **Structure**:
 
 
• The C60 structure is made up of 60 carbon atoms that are linked together to form a hollow cage.
 
• The construction has 32 facets, 20 of which are hexagons and 12 of which are pentagons.
 
• No two pentagons have the same vertex.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The property of an element which exists in more than one physical form is called allotrope and the forms are called **allotrope**.

 
 
• **Carbon **shows allotropy due to chaining, which is the joining of atoms of the same element to each other to form long chains.
 
• Various allotropes of carbon exist in nature, including **diamond, graphene, fullerene, C60, C70, amorphous carbon, Cu carbon, Lonsdaleite, and carbon nanotubes**.
 
 
• **Diamond**
 
 
• ​The structure of diamond is tetrahedral.
 
• Each carbon atom is linked to four other carbon atoms by covalent bonds to form a giant crystal lattice.
 
• Due to its tetrahedral structure, diamond is one of the hardest known materials.
 
• It has a high refractive index, reflects light internally and hence shines.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Graphene**:
 
 
• ​It is a single-layer compound derived from graphite.
 
• In its hexagonal lattice, each carbon is bonded to three others, giving up an extra electron.
 
• Graphene is an excellent conductor of electricity and heat due to its extra electrons.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:

(i) Diamond is hard and graphite is soft.

(ii) Diamond is soft and graphite is hard.

(iii) Diamond is a bad conductor and graphite is a good conductor.

(iv) Diamond is a good conductor and graphite is a bad conductor.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**(i) and (iii)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Diamond is the **hardest naturally occurring material** due to its strong covalent bonding and tetrahedral structure.
 
• Graphite is soft because of its layered structure, where layers are held together by weak van der Waals forces, allowing them to slide over one another.
 
• Diamond is an **electrical insulator** because it lacks free electrons for conductivity.
 
• Graphite is a **good conductor of electricity** due to the presence of delocalized electrons within its layers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Allotropes of Carbon:**

 
 
• Carbon exists in different forms known as allotropes, such as diamond, graphite, graphene, and fullerene.
 
• These allotropes have distinct physical and chemical properties due to differences in their atomic arrangements.
 
 
 
• **Structure of Diamond:**
 
 
• Diamond has a three-dimensional tetrahedral structure where each carbon atom is covalently bonded to four other carbon atoms.
 
• This structure makes diamond extremely hard and gives it a high melting point.
 
 
 
• **Structure of Graphite:**
 
 
• Graphite has a planar structure consisting of layers of carbon atoms arranged in hexagonal rings.
 
• The layers are held together by weak van der Waals forces, allowing them to slide, making graphite a lubricant.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• Diamond is used in cutting tools, drill bits, and jewelry due to its hardness and brilliance.
 
• Graphite is used in pencils, lubricants, and as electrodes in batteries due to its conductivity.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct name of a carbon compound with three-carbon chains and a ketone group?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Propanone__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The **IUPAC name** of CH₃COCH₃ is **propanone** as the suffix used for the ketone group is **-one** and propane because the parent chain consists of** three carbon**.
 
• **The structural formula of propane is: **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f6f74d58ff28484cb2f9bac087c01b1b11bcf5441c144fed3afe296a9ab072cf.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Preparation of Propanone**:

 
 
• 2CH≡CH + 3H₂O +Mg (at 420°C) → CH₃COCH₃+ CO₂ +2H₂ ​
 
• From the above reaction, propanone can be prepared from ethyne by passing a mixture of ethyne and stream over a catalyst, magnesium at 420℃.
 
 
 
• **Propanol:** 
 
 
• It consists of** 3 carbon chain and 1 alcohol group (-OH bond)** 
 
• Chemical formula: **CH₃CH₂CH₂OH.**
 
 
 
• **Propanal:**
 
 
• It consists of **3 carbon chain and 1 aldehyde. **
 
• Chemical formula: **CH₃CH₂CHO**.
 
 
 
• **Propene: ** 
 
 
• It consists of **3 carbon chain and 1 double bond in between 2 carbons.**
 
• Chemical formula: **CH₃CH=CH₂ .**

questions.question: Fullerene consists of _____ carbon atoms.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**60**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fullerenes** are a class of carbon allotropes.
 
• The most well-known fullerene is the **C₆₀** molecule, also known as **Buckminsterfullerene**.
 
• The **C₆₀** molecule consists of **60 carbon atoms** arranged in a structure that resembles a **soccer ball**, with a mix of hexagonal and pentagonal rings.
 
• The structure of **C₆₀** is highly symmetric and is known as a **truncated icosahedron**.
 
• **Fullerenes** were discovered in **1985** by **Sir Harold Kroto, Richard Smalley, and Robert Curl**, who were awarded the **Nobel Prize in Chemistry** in **1996** for this discovery.
 
• Fullerenes have unique **chemical and physical properties** and have potential applications in **nanotechnology, materials science, and electronics**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option 1: 32**__

 __
 
• 32 is not a characteristic number of carbon atoms in any well-known fullerene structure.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: 48**__
 __
 
• 48 is also not a characteristic number of carbon atoms in any well-known fullerene structure.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: 4**__
 
 
• 4 carbon atoms are characteristic of smaller carbon compounds like methane (CH₄), not fullerenes.

questions.question: Compounds with exactly two double carbon–carbon bonds are known as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dienes.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A molecule called diene **has** two double bonds between its carbon** atoms and is **unsaturated.**
 
• **Diene** is employed in industry as a** complex polymer's monomer constituent.** 
 
• It is also used in **Organic Synthesis.**
 
• Dienes are divided into** three groups** based on where the** double bond is located **relative to the rest of the molecule:
 
 
• A **cumulated diene** is one that has **two consecutive double bonds** on nearby Carbon atoms. They go by the name** Allene too.**
 
• A **conjugated diene** is a compound with **two conjugated double bonds** that are spaced apart by just** one bond.**
 
• **Two double bonds** that are spaced apart by** two or more double bond**s make up an** isolated diene.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Terpenes:**

 
 
• Terpenes are a group of **organic compounds** with the formula** (C₅H₈)n,** where **n is greater than 1. **
 
 
 
• **Alkyne:**
 
 
• Alkynes are hydrocarbons that have **triple bonds between carbon atoms.**
 
• When it comes to** molecules with one triple bond**, their usual formula is **CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ (and no rings).**

questions.question: With which of the following does the hydrophilic end of soaps react?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Water:**
 
• The hydrophilic end of a soap molecule is the polar end.
 
• This end is attracted to water molecules because water is also a polar molecule.
 
• "Hydrophilic" literally means "water-loving."
 
• The hydrophilic end of the soap molecule contains a negatively charged carboxylate group (COO-) or a similar ionic group.
 
• This charged end interacts strongly with the polar water molecules through ion-dipole interactions and hydrogen bonding.
 
• This interaction allows soap to dissolve in water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hydrocarbon:**
 
• Hydrocarbons are non-polar molecules.
 
• The hydrophobic end of a soap molecule, which is the long hydrocarbon chain, interacts with hydrocarbons.
 
• This non-polar end is repelled by water.
 
• Hydrocarbons are oil based molecules.
 
• The hydrocarbon chain is what allows soaps to interact with grease and oil.
 
• **Oil:**
 
• The hydrophobic end of a soap molecule interacts with oil.
 
• This end is non-polar and is repelled by water.
 
• The hydrophobic end is the long hydrocarbon chain.
 
• This is how soap removes oils and greases.
 
• The oil is surrounded by the hydrophobic ends, and the hydrophilic ends interact with the water, allowing the oil to be washed away.

questions.question: Which Carbon Compound is used as fire extinguisher?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**CCI4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Carbon tetrachloride (CCI4)** is commonly used in fire extinguishers, particularly in older models.
 
• CCI4 is effective in extinguishing fires because it is a non-flammable liquid that can inhibit the chemical reactions occurring in a flame.
 
• It was extensively used in fire extinguishers designed for electrical fires and liquid fires (Class B and C fires).
 
• Despite its effectiveness, the use of CCI4 has declined due to its toxic and potentially carcinogenic effects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Fire Extinguishers**

 
 
• **Water Extinguishers**: Used for Class A fires involving ordinary combustibles like wood and paper.
 
• **Foam Extinguishers**: Effective on Class A and B fires involving flammable liquids.
 
• **Dry Powder Extinguishers**: Suitable for Class A, B, and C fires, used for a wide range of fire types.
 
• **CO2 Extinguishers**: Ideal for electrical fires and flammable liquid fires (Class B and C).
 
 
 
• **Fire Extinguisher Classes**
 
 
• **Class A**: Fires involving solid combustibles like wood, paper, and textiles.
 
• **Class B**: Fires involving flammable liquids such as petrol and paint.
 
• **Class C**: Fires involving gases like propane and butane.
 
• **Class D**: Fires involving metals such as magnesium and aluminum.
 
• **Class K**: Fires involving cooking oils and fats.
 
 
 
• **Health Risks of CCI4**
 
 
• CCI4 can cause liver and kidney damage upon prolonged exposure.
 
• It is classified as a probable human carcinogen by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC).
 
• Inhalation of CCI4 vapors can lead to central nervous system depression.
 
 
 
• **Modern Fire Extinguishers**
 
 
• Due to the health risks associated with CCI4, modern fire extinguishers use less toxic and more environmentally friendly agents.
 
• Halons and Halocarbons are commonly used in place of CCI4 for electrical and flammable liquid fires.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT a reason for the versatile nature of carbon?

options.text: Carbon can form ionic bonds with itself
Carbon can form single, double, and triple bonds

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Carbon atoms do not typically form ionic bonds with themselves; they primarily form covalent bonds.
 
• Ionic bonds are formed between metals and non-metals, whereas carbon, being a non-metal, forms covalent bonds.
 
• The versatile nature of carbon is attributed to its ability to form stable covalent bonds with a variety of other elements, including itself.
 
• Carbon's capability to catenate, or form long chains and rings with other carbon atoms, is due to its covalent bonding nature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tetravalency**:

 
 
• Carbon has four valence electrons, allowing it to form four covalent bonds with other atoms.
 
• This property enables carbon to form complex and diverse organic molecules.
 
 
 
• **Catenation**:
 
 
• Carbon atoms can bond with each other to form long chains, branched structures, and rings.
 
• This property is unique among elements and contributes to the complexity of organic chemistry.
 
 
 
• **Bond Types**:
 
 
• Carbon can form single, double, and triple bonds with other carbon atoms and with other elements.
 
• This versatility in bonding types allows for the formation of a wide variety of organic compounds.
 
 
 
• **Hybridization**:
 
 
• Carbon can undergo sp, sp2, and sp3 hybridization, leading to different geometrical structures of molecules.
 
• Hybridization allows carbon to form linear, trigonal planar, and tetrahedral structures.

questions.question: Which of the following carbon allotropes is amorphous?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lampblack**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Lampblack** is a form of carbon that is produced by the incomplete combustion of heavy petroleum products.
 
• It is classified as an **amorphous** carbon allotrope, meaning it lacks a well-defined crystalline structure.
 
• It is primarily used as a pigment in inks, paints, and coatings, as well as in rubber products.
 
• Lampblack is also known as **carbon black** and has excellent tinting strength and stability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Diamond**

 
 
• It is a crystalline allotrope of carbon known for its hardness and high refractive index.
 
• Diamonds are used in jewelry and industrial cutting tools.
 
 
 
• **Fullerenes**
 
 
• These are molecules composed entirely of carbon, taking the form of a hollow sphere, ellipsoid, or tube.
 
• Buckminsterfullerene (C60) is the most well-known fullerene, resembling a soccer ball.
 
 
 
• **Graphite**
 
 
• Graphite is another crystalline form of carbon where atoms are arranged in a hexagonal lattice.
 
• It is used in pencils, lubricants, and as a moderator in nuclear reactors.
 
 
 
• **Amorphous Carbon**
 
 
• Amorphous carbon is a form of carbon that does not have any crystalline structure.
 
• Examples include lampblack, coal, and charcoal.
